findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row aborts the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) on parse and return Result

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into Vec from split
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma-separated field causes panic via index-out-of-bounds

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: pure core logic leaks side effects; function cannot be tested deterministically and logging escapes the imperative shell boundary

findings.problem: load_packets performs I/O (fs::read_to_string) and logging mixed with data parsing in a single function
findings.failure_mode: functional core is not separated from imperative shell; cannot unit-test parsing logic without real filesystem access
findings.fix: split into parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (pure core) and load_packets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> (shell that reads file and delegates to core)

findings.problem: text.lines().map(...).collect() allocates unbounded Vec<String> from unbounded file input without try_reserve or row cap
findings.failure_mode: large input file exhausts memory or causes allocation failure panic
findings.fix: parse with split_once, enforce a maximum row count, preflight result storage with try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| AllocationError)?, and push with bounded checks

findings.problem: .to_string() allocates a new String for every CSV field without any cap
findings.failure_mode: each field heap-allocates; large or numerous rows cause excessive memory pressure and allocation failure
findings.fix: pass &str into the Record type or use a bounded field cap with try_reserve on the field Vec; better yet use Cow<str> or accept &str at the boundary

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 instead of domain newtypes or typed value objects
findings.failure_mode: any code can construct Record with empty name, negative value, or otherwise invalid data; illegal states are representable
findings.fix: introduce Name(newtype String with validation), validated value type, and a fallible constructor like Record::new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, ParseError>

findings.problem: raw primitives (String, u16 from parsing) enter the domain through public struct fields without a parse boundary/smart constructor
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct invalid states directly bypassing validation
findings.fix: make Record fields private, provide only a fallible constructor that validates invariants, and use private fields with newtype wrappers

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures surface as panics via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: no caller can distinguish between I/O error, parse error, overflow, or structural error; all failures are unrecoverable crashes
findings.fix: define a domain error enum (e.g. LoadError { Io(IoError), Parse(ParseError), Overflow, Empty }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>
